title: Measuring Magnetic Actuation in Monolayer Vanadium-Doped WS2 Using In-Situ Lorentz TEM
content: The rapidly growing field of two-dimensional (2D) magnetic materials has necessitated sensitive nanoscale magnetic imaging techniques that can resolve weak signals and small features in atomically thin systems. Though many optical methods, such as magneto-optical Kerr effect [1], magnetic circular dichroism [2], and second harmonic generation [3], have successfully characterized 2D magnetic ordering, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy (Lorentz TEM), which has significantly better diffraction-limited spatial resolution, has not yet been well-explored at the single-layer limit due to the rapidly diminishing magnetic phase contrast as sample thickness decreases. Here we investigate Lorentz TEM contrast arising from monolayer vanadium-doped WS2, a room-temperature, carrier-mediated ferromagnetic semiconductor [4]. Rather than observing conventional domain boundary contrast in Fresnel Lorentz TEM, we find that the low bending energy of monolayer materials enables out-of-plane deformation due to torque from the in-situ applied magnetic field. We measure the bending angle of the monolayer films and determine the effects of electron dose and temperature on the actuation response.
